# `silk/core/reflect`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

Compile-time descriptions of the fields of a struct or tuple type, for generic code that visits
each field.

## When to use
Use [`Reflect`](#Reflect) to write one generic function that works on the fields of many types, such as a
serializer or a formatter. Use [`Reflect.fields`](#Reflect.impl.fields) with `static for` to visit each field, and
[`Reflect.borrowField`](#Reflect.impl.borrowField) to read the value of a field at runtime, or [`Reflect.borrowFieldMut`](#Reflect.impl.borrowFieldMut)
to change it.

## Details
Descriptors exist only during static evaluation. They have no runtime value, so reflection adds
no runtime cost. The compiler expands a `static for` over [`Reflect.fields`](#Reflect.impl.fields) into one copy of
the loop body for each field, in declaration order. In each copy, the field has its own type.

A descriptor shows only the fields that are visible from the module that calls the reflection
operation. Private fields of a type from another module are not in the list.

## Examples
### Add all fields of a struct
```silk
import silk.core.reflect { Reflect }

struct Pair {
  pub first: i32,
  pub second: i32,
}

fn sum(owner: &Pair) -> i32 {
  let mut total = 0
  static for field in Reflect.fields<Pair>() {
    total = total + Reflect.borrowField<Pair, i32>(owner, field).*
  }
  return total
}

pub fn main() -> i32 {
  let pair = Pair { first: 20, second: 22 }
  if sum(&pair) != 42 {
    return 1
  }
  return 0
}
```

Import as `Reflect` with `import silk.core.reflect { Reflect }`.


<a id="Reflect"></a>

## `Reflect`

```silk
pub struct Reflect
```

The owner type of the reflection operations. It has no fields and is never constructed.

### Details

Each operation except [`Reflect.borrowField`](#Reflect.impl.borrowField) and [`Reflect.borrowFieldMut`](#Reflect.impl.borrowFieldMut) is `static`. It
runs only during static evaluation, such as in a `static for`, a `static if`, or a `static fn`.

<a id="Reflect.impl.typeOf"></a>

### Associated function `typeOf`

```silk
pub static fn typeOf<Owner>() -> Intrinsic.Type<Owner>
```

Returns the compile-time descriptor of the struct or tuple type `Owner`.

#### Details

Give the descriptor to [`Reflect.typeKind`](#Reflect.impl.typeKind) to find the kind of type.

<a id="Reflect.impl.fields"></a>

### Associated function `fields`

```silk
pub static fn fields<Owner>() -> Intrinsic.Fields<Owner>
```

Returns the compile-time descriptors of the fields of `Owner`, in declaration order.

#### Details

Use the result as the sequence of a `static for`. Each element has the type
`Intrinsic.Field<Owner, Value>`, where `Value` is the type of that field.

#### Gotchas

The list contains only the `pub` fields, even when the caller is the module that declares
`Owner`, because visibility is judged from `silk/core/reflect`. Call `Intrinsic.reflectFields<Owner>()`
directly to list the fields that the calling module can see.

<a id="Reflect.impl.typeKind"></a>

### Associated function `typeKind`

```silk
pub static fn typeKind<Owner>(descriptor: Intrinsic.Type<Owner>) -> u8
```

Returns the kind of type that `descriptor` describes: [`namedKind`](#namedKind), [`positionalKind`](#positionalKind),
[`anonymousNamedKind`](#anonymousNamedKind), [`anonymousPositionalKind`](#anonymousPositionalKind), [`arrayKind`](#arrayKind), or [`otherKind`](#otherKind). Every
type has a kind, so a generic function can branch on the kind of its type parameter.

<a id="Reflect.impl.borrowField"></a>

### Associated function `borrowField`

```silk
pub fn borrowField<Owner, Value>(owner: &Owner, static field: Intrinsic.Field<Owner, Value>) -> &Value
```

Returns a shared borrow of the field of `owner` that `field` describes.

#### Details

`field` is a static argument, so the compiler selects the field during specialization. At
runtime this function is a plain field access. The borrow lives as long as the borrow of
`owner`.

#### Gotchas

`field` must come from [`Reflect.fields`](#Reflect.impl.fields) for the same `Owner` type. This function cannot move
a field out of an owned value.

<a id="Reflect.impl.borrowFieldMut"></a>

### Associated function `borrowFieldMut`

```silk
pub fn borrowFieldMut<Owner, Value>(owner: &mut Owner, static field: Intrinsic.Field<Owner, Value>) -> &mut Value
```

Returns a mutable borrow of the field of `owner` that `field` describes.

#### Details

`field` is a static argument, so the compiler selects the field during specialization. At
runtime this function is a plain field access. The borrow lives as long as the mutable borrow
of `owner`, and `owner` cannot be used while the field borrow is live.

#### Examples

```silk
import silk.core.reflect { Reflect }

struct Counters {
  pub hits: i32,
  pub misses: i32,
}

fn reset(counters: &mut Counters) -> () {
  static for field in Reflect.fields<Counters>() {
    let place = Reflect.borrowFieldMut<Counters, i32>(&mut counters.*, field)
    place.* = 0
  }
  return ()
}

pub fn main() -> i32 {
  let mut counters = Counters { hits: 4, misses: 2 }
  reset(&mut counters)
  return counters.hits + counters.misses
}
```

#### Gotchas

`field` must come from [`Reflect.fields`](#Reflect.impl.fields) for the same `Owner` type. `owner` must be a mutable
borrow; a shared borrow is refused.

<a id="Reflect.impl.variants"></a>

### Associated function `variants`

```silk
pub static fn variants<Union>() -> Intrinsic.Variants<Union>
```

Returns the compile-time descriptors of the variants of the nominal union `Union`, in
declaration order.

#### Details

Use the result as the sequence of a `static for`. Each element has the type
`Intrinsic.Variant<Union>`. Give it to [`Reflect.variantLabel`](#Reflect.impl.variantLabel), [`Reflect.variantFields`](#Reflect.impl.variantFields),
[`Reflect.makeVariant`](#Reflect.impl.makeVariant) or [`Reflect.isVariant`](#Reflect.impl.isVariant).

#### Examples

```silk
import silk.core.option { Option }
import silk.core.reflect { Reflect }

union Command {
  Status,
  Clone { pub url: string, pub depth: u32 },
}

static fn fieldCount<U>(variant: Intrinsic.Variant<U>) -> usize {
  let mut count: usize = 0
  static for field in Reflect.variantFields(variant) { count = count + 1 }
  return count
}

// Builds the variant of `U` named `word`, if it has no fields.
fn unitNamed<U>(word: string) -> Option<U> {
  static for variant in Reflect.variants<U>() {
    static if fieldCount(variant) == 0 {
      if word == Reflect.variantLabel(variant) {
        return Option<U>.some(Reflect.makeVariant(variant, ()))
      }
    }
  }
  return Option<U>.none()
}

pub fn main() -> i32 {
  let found = unitNamed<Command>("Status")
  return match move found {
    Option<Command>.Some {value: Command.Status} => 0
    _ => 1
  }
}
```


Returns the name of a variant, as written in the union declaration.

<a id="Reflect.impl.variantFields"></a>

### Associated function `variantFields`

```silk
pub static fn variantFields<Union>(variant: Intrinsic.Variant<Union>) -> Intrinsic.Fields<Union>
```

Returns the compile-time descriptors of the fields of a variant, in declaration order.

#### Details

Each element has the type `Intrinsic.Field<Union, Value>`, where `Value` is the type of that
field, and the kind [`variantFieldKind`](#variantFieldKind). A unit variant has none.

#### Gotchas

The list contains only the `pub` fields, because visibility is judged from `silk/core/reflect`.
A field descriptor of a variant cannot be given to [`Reflect.borrowField`](#Reflect.impl.borrowField), because the
union holds the field only while that variant is active.

<a id="Reflect.impl.makeVariant"></a>

### Associated function `makeVariant`

```silk
pub fn makeVariant<Union, Fields>(static variant: Intrinsic.Variant<Union>, fields: Fields) -> Union
```

Returns the variant that `variant` describes, built from `fields`: a tuple of the variant's
fields in declaration order, or `()` for a variant without fields.

#### Details

`variant` is a static argument, so the compiler selects the variant during specialization.
At runtime this function is a plain variant construction, such as
`Shape.Line {length: a, width: b}` for `makeVariant(line, (a, b))`. The tuple is
moved into the variant.

#### Examples

```silk
import silk.core.reflect { Reflect }

union Shape {
  Dot,
  Circle { pub radius: u32 },
  Line { pub length: u32, pub width: u32 },
}

fn area(shape: Shape) -> u32 {
  return match move shape {
    Shape.Dot => 0
    Shape.Circle {radius} => radius * radius * 3
    Shape.Line {length, width} => length * width
  }
}

static fn fieldCount<U>(variant: Intrinsic.Variant<U>) -> usize {
  let mut count: usize = 0
  static for field in Reflect.variantFields(variant) { count = count + 1 }
  return count
}

pub fn main() -> i32 {
  let two: u32 = 2
  let three: u32 = 3
  let four: u32 = 4
  let mut total: u32 = 0
  static for variant in Reflect.variants<Shape>() {
    let static count = fieldCount(variant)
    static if count == 0 { total = total + area(Reflect.makeVariant(variant, ())) }
    static if count == 1 { total = total + area(Reflect.makeVariant(variant, (two,))) }
    static if count == 2 { total = total + area(Reflect.makeVariant(variant, (three, four))) }
  }
  // 0 + 12 + 12
  if total != 24 {
    return 1
  }
  return 0
}
```

#### Gotchas

The tuple must have exactly the variant's field types in declaration order. Every field of the
variant must be `pub`, since the variant is built from `silk/core/reflect`.

<a id="Reflect.impl.isVariant"></a>

### Associated function `isVariant`

```silk
pub fn isVariant<Union>(owner: &Union, static variant: Intrinsic.Variant<Union>) -> bool
```

Returns whether `owner` holds the variant that `variant` describes.

#### Details

`variant` is a static argument, so at runtime this function is a plain test of the union's
active variant, like a `match` with one arm for that variant.
